correctness.rationale: For independent Haar variables the two regular a classes each map bijectively and at every residue level onto 3Z_3 via the unit derivative of T. On the critical class T=(9A²−1)/8. This gives masses 1/9, 4/9, 4/9 for critical–critical, mixed and regular–regular. When n=1 mod 3 only the first branch fails. When n=2 mod 3 only the first can work; there it has valuation one unless n=8 mod 9. In the exceptional branch division by the square 9/64 and the Haar-preserving unit change B→B sqrt(1−9A²) give Q((64n+1)/9). For 3|n the first branch contributes 1/9, the mixed branch contributes (4/9)(1/8) and the regular–regular branch can contribute only for 9|n, then via H. For Q, counting nonzero coordinates modulo 3, with uniform Haar distribution on the zero-output class when a derivative is a unit, gives Q(1 mod 3)=1/6, Q(2 mod 3)=1/2, Q(valuation one)=4/9 and Q(c)=4/9+Q(c/9)/9 for 9|c, including c=0. For H, independence and convolution give w_j. At equal valuations exactly half the unit additions cancel, leaving uniform 3Z_3; their square probabilities after multiplying by 3^k are 1/8 for even k and 3/8 for odd k. The other half has residue twice the unit of m and is square exactly if k is even and that unit is 2. This yields the three beta values; unequal valuations and the m=0 sum give the other terms. Zero is included in the event and does not affect continuous shell calculations. Compactness and decreasing-set continuity justify passing from the modular probabilities to the Haar probability. Independently enumerated ordered pairs through modulus 729 for ten shifts including 0 and negative shifts and bounded the difference between finite square-existence and the formula by the mass of the zero residue; a separate replay also checks the nine reference outputs and 405 nested counts through modulus 243.
residual_risks: The finite enumeration corroborates the local probabilities but does not establish any all-integer global Diophantine statement or replace the all-parameter proof.

evidence: Triangular D(n) pairs express the same square equation; the zero-shift Pi(k,j) is four times the triangular product. The Resultary obstruction 8840d7811f36 gives an iff for solvability in all finite moduli for positive shifts.
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: Multiplication by four does not change squareness, but a construction, a no-solution obstruction or even the full solvability census does not give the fraction of Haar-uniform pairs. The limiting proportion of pairs admitting at least one modular root, not the number of roots, is the equivalent probabilistic formulation.

originality.rationale: Credit is for the explicit all-shift square-value Haar probabilities, including Q and H, not for the already documented obstruction at n=2,5 mod 9 or the classical square criterion. The closest available statements determine solvability or construct particular integral pairs, not probability under uniform independent free indices. The comparison is bounded by the examined texts and indexed results.
residual_risks: An unindexed equivalent Haar formula or an implicit specialization of general p-adic integration machinery remains possible; the exact Yang formulas were not inspected.

value.rationale: This is a natural quantitative local refinement of the known obstruction in a Diophantine pair problem. It separates admissible shifts by actual probability, explains singular variation via valuations and terminal units, and determines the limiting residue-pair proportion for every shift rather than merely giving a witness or one tested modulus. Distinguishing root existence from representation counts is needed to interpret that invariant.
residual_risks: Does not predict the frequency of integral positive pairs or provide a local-to-global principle.
